concept.body: Density = mass ÷ volume identifies materials (steel ≈ 7.8, water 1, pine 0.6 g/cm³); mass = density × volume cashes out every volume formula in grams. An object floats when its AVERAGE density (mass over total outer volume, hollows included) is below the fluid's — and density never changes under scaling (mass and volume both take k³).

widget.prompt: A solid cube of side 3 cm has mass 54 g. Density (g/cm³) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 18 = 54/3 divides by the side — volume is 27: density 2.

steps.body: Volume meets matter through **density = mass ÷ volume**. A material's density is its identity card — steel ≈ 7.8 g/cm³, water 1, pine 0.6 — so mass = density × volume turns every formula this course justified into a WEIGHT prediction, and density < 1 predicts floating.

widget.prompt: A solid steel sphere (radius 3 cm, density 7.8 g/cm³). Mass (nearest gram) = ?

numericErrors.feedback: 113 is the VOLUME (36π) — multiply by the density 7.8: ≈ 882 g.
2646 uses V = 4πr³ (dropping the /3): 108π × 7.8 — the sphere holds (4/3)π(27) = 36π ≈ 113.1: mass ≈ 882.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: 7.8 × 36π ≈ 882 g — the justified formula, cashed out in grams.
widget.successFeedback: 7.8 × 36π ≈ 882 g — the justified formula, cashed out in grams.

widget.prompt: A solid cube of side 4 cm has mass 512 g. Its density (g/cm³) = ?

numericErrors.feedback: 128 = 512/4 divides by the SIDE — divide by the volume 4³ = 64: density 8.
32 = 512/16 divides by a FACE — the volume is 64: 8.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: 512 ÷ 64 = 8 g/cm³ — mass and geometry naming the material together.
widget.successFeedback: 512 ÷ 64 = 8 g/cm³ — mass and geometry naming the material together.

explanationVariants: Floating compares the OBJECT's average density to water's 1.

widget.prompt: A solid pine block (density 0.6 g/cm³) of ANY shape is placed in water (density 1). It:

options.label: Floats — average density below water's, regardless of shape or size
options.feedback: The float test is a pure density comparison; geometry decides HOW HIGH it rides, not whether.

options.label: Sinks if it's large enough
options.feedback: Size scales mass and displaced water TOGETHER (both k³) — the ratio 0.6 never changes.

options.label: Floats only as a flat plank
options.feedback: Shape is style, density is verdict: 0.6 < 1 floats in any pose.

options.label: Depends on the water's depth
options.feedback: Depth is irrelevant to the comparison — 0.6 vs 1 settles it.

widget.prompt: A designer needs a 3 by 3 by 4 block. Build it, then read its volume — density will turn that volume into a mass.

commonBuilds.feedback: 9 is the 3 × 3 base. The block is 4 tall, so multiply by 4.
12 is 3 × 4, one face. All three dimensions multiply: 3 × 3 × 4.

widget.successFeedback: 36 cubic units. Density is mass per unit volume, so this single number is what a density figure gets multiplied by — change the shape and the mass follows.
widget.lowFeedback: Fewer cubes than the designer asked for — grow toward 3 by 3 by 4.
widget.highFeedback: More cubes than the designer asked for — shrink toward 3 by 3 by 4.

widget.prompt: A solid statue is scaled up by k = 4 in the same material. Its density:

options.label: Unchanged — mass and volume both grow ×64, and their ratio cancels
options.feedback: Density is a material property, size-blind: k³ over k³ = 1.
Both mass and volume take k³ — the ratio holds.
That's the MASS factor alone — volume matches it, so density is constant.
Nothing dilutes — same material, same density.

hints: Archimedes' original problem: compare the crown's density to gold's.
Gold runs 19.3 — does the crown measure up?
explanationVariants: 3700/200 = 18.5 < 19.3 — the crown is NOT pure gold: something lighter is alloyed in. Enter 18.5.

widget.prompt: A 'gold' crown has mass 3700 g and displaces 200 cm³ of water. Pure gold's density is 19.3 g/cm³. The crown's measured density = ?

numericErrors.feedback: 19.3 is PURE gold's card — this crown measures 3700/200 = 18.5: adulterated.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: 3700 ÷ 200 = 18.5 < 19.3 — Archimedes' verdict by division: not pure.
widget.successFeedback: 3700 ÷ 200 = 18.5 < 19.3 — Archimedes' verdict by division: not pure.

takeaways: Density = mass ÷ volume: the material's identity card (steel 7.8, water 1, pine 0.6).
Mass = density × justified volume; float when average density < 1 (hollowing lowers it — ships).
Density is scale-invariant: k³ over k³.
